Man Buys New 2026 Ford F-150 Raptor R for $117,520, Drives 2,200 Miles, Sells for $118,000
28 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
Remember when you could buy a brand-new F-150 Raptor R, drive it around for a few months, and then sell it for considerably more than what you originally paid? Well, it's possible those days might be coming to an end, even though we've seen several examples exchanging hands for over MSRP in recent months. Let's just say this: mileage matters.
You know I've been keeping a close eye on these things for a while now. Not just the Raptor R, but also the C8 Corvette, all the Hellcat variants, and so on.
The "problem" with the Raptor R has always been availability. Ford dealers don't exactly have dozens of these babies sitting around waiting for customers, and securing an allocation can be difficult. Still, there's a difference between holding your value and going up in value. Let's take this particular 2026 Raptor R for example.
It was purchased new by its original owner for $117,520, driven for roughly 2,200 miles, and then listed at auction with no reserve. The winning bid turned out to be $118,000 (plus a buyer's fee), meaning the seller technically got $480 over MSRP for it. Purely from a depreciation standpoint, that's a pretty spectacular result, I don't care where you're from!
In terms of specs, this Raptor R comes with an Antimatter Blue Metallic exterior, which I think looks fantastic - especially compared to some of the more common colorways you can get on a flagship F-150. Actually, I'm not going to downplay this, because I think this color might just be my favorite Raptor R hue ever. Not gonna lie. What do you guys think about the spec?
Other highlights include the model-specific vented hood, Code Orange tow hooks, R badges, LED headlights, Rigid LED fog lights, side mirror lighting, a dual-panel sunroof, power-operated tailgate, tonneau cover, and a receiver hitch.
Meanwhile, the 17" forged beadlock-capable wheels come wrapped in BFGoodrich KO2 all-terrain rubber, while the suspension features Fox dual live-valve shocks. You also get Ford's Terrain Management System and Trail Control, so this thing is obviously more than just a straight-line beast.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Moving along to the interior, that's where you'll find the heated and ventilated front Recaro bucket seats, a heated 60/40 split-folding rear bench, Black Alcantara suede and leather upholstery, carbon fiber trim, a 14-speaker Bang & Olufsen sound system, Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, a wireless charging pad, a heated and leather-wrapped steering wheel, a 360-degree camera system, and more.
As for the engine, it's a supercharged 5.2-liter Predator V8 , not unlike what you'd find in a Mustang Shelby GT500 (albeit with a smaller supercharger pulley and revised software). The factory output is 720 horsepower and 640 lb-ft of torque, with everything getting sent to all four wheels via a 10-speed automatic transmission.
